caption:
Austin’s wildfire protection plan is back before City Council this week.

A briefing is scheduled for October 20, followed by a proposed vote October 22 on adopting the updated Austin–Travis County Community Wildfire Protection Plan.

The plan brings together local departments, partner agencies and community input to identify wildfire risks and ways to reduce them. City staff says the Texas A&M Forest Service approved the update on July 13, 2026; formal City Council adoption is the next step now on the agenda.

Why homeowners should pay attention: The draft resolution says an approved plan supports eligibility to pursue Community Wildfire Defense Grants and other funding to carry out its recommendations.

Adoption would establish a planning framework. This agenda item does not itself allocate new spending, and the proposal should not be read as a new property-specific insurance requirement or a guarantee of funding.

For Austin-area owners and buyers, it’s a local housing issue worth following: how the community prepares to protect homes and neighborhoods.

Sources: City of Austin, October 20 work-session agenda and October 22 Council Item 11; supporting documents posted October 16, 2026.
